🔎 DefectSpotter

Visual inspection without defect labels. A quality inspector at the end of the line uploads a part image (or a batch); DefectSpotter compares it with what good parts look like, returns an anomaly score, a heat map of the suspected defect and a PASS / CHECK / REJECT decision — trained without a single defect image. Products: bottle, screw, carpet.

1 · The business problem

Factories rarely have many images of defects: most parts are good, defects are rare, varied and keep changing. A supervised classifier needs hundreds of labelled examples per defect type — a new scratch pattern it has never seen simply passes.

Two errors cost money in opposite directions:

  • Escape (missed defect): a defective part reaches the customer → complaints, warranty, recalls.
  • False reject: a good part is scrapped or reworked → material, throughput and inspector time.
User. A quality inspector at the end of a production line.
Idea. Learn the appearance of good parts only; flag anything unusual and show where it is.
Output. Anomaly score (0–100), heat map, suspected regions and a PASS / CHECK / REJECT decision; CHECK goes to a human.
Operating point. A threshold slider exposes the trade-off between false rejects and escapes; the default is chosen with synthetic defects and an explicit cost model.

PatchCore-style detector

A frozen ImageNet ResNet-18 (one shared 11 MB ONNX file) turns the image into a grid of patch descriptors (layer2 + layer3). Each product gets its own recipe, chosen without real defects: input resolution, 3×3 neighbourhood averaging vs raw descriptors that keep fine weave detail, and pose normalisation for parts that arrive in any orientation (every screw rotated to the same pose). Descriptors of all good training parts form a memory bank, compressed with greedy k-center coreset selection. A test patch far from every normal patch is anomalous; the largest distance is the image score. No training of the network is needed — onboarding a product takes seconds.

Variational autoencoders (Generative AI)

A VAE learns to rebuild good parts through a small random latent code; it cannot rebuild a defect, so the reconstruction error highlights it. The feature-space VAE (v3) rebuilds the CNN's feature map through a 32×7×7 spatial latent and is the generative detector; the pixel VAE (v1, 128-d latent, L1 + SSIM) is kept for comparison — its blurry reconstructions show why working in feature space matters.

Classical baseline

Images are aligned to a median good reference with OpenCV ECC (translation / rigid / affine chosen automatically), then compared with the per-pixel mean and standard deviation of good parts. Transparent and fast — and it shows exactly where learned features are needed (rotating screws, textures).

Synthetic defects choose the threshold

Held-out good parts are corrupted with procedural cut-paste, scratch and stain defects (with exact masks), refined by Stable Diffusion (SDEdit image-to-image) for realistic texture. Every synthetic defect is also replayed at 25% and 50% severity — the "detection limit" a real inspection spec defines — because full-strength synthetic defects are far more conspicuous than real thread damage on screws. A set only joins the default calibration if the detector reliably separates it from good parts (synthetic AUROC ≥ 0.9); weaker sets document the detection limit. With held-out good parts they (1) set the 0–100 score scale (25 = typical good, 75 = typical synthetic defect), (2) tune hyper-parameters and (3) pick the cost-optimal PASS/CHECK/REJECT thresholds — no real defect is used. Real defects only measure how close that threshold is to an oracle chosen with labels.

Built to mirror a real line

  • Cost model: 1% prevalence, escape ≫ false reject, inspector time per CHECK, review capacity ≤ 10% of parts, planned at ≤ 50% utilisation (headroom for lot-to-lot drift).
  • Acquisition health gate: if brightness / contrast / focus is outside the qualified range, no automatic decision is taken - PASS or REJECT becomes CHECK (no blind shipping, no scrapping good parts under bad light).
  • Human review queue + audit log for every CHECK; the model never silently retrains.
  • Leakage-free splits: model-fit good · calibration good · oracle-threshold test · operating test.
  • Few-shot onboarding of a new product (metal nut) from a handful of good parts.

What the EDA tells us

  • Tiny defects dominate: 45% of labelled defects cover less than 1% of the image (median 1.48%). Down-scaling is therefore a real risk, which is why localisation metrics (pixel AUROC, AUPRO) are reported next to image AUROC.
  • bottle: 900×900 px, brightness 137±2, sharpness 188±34.
  • carpet: 1024×1024 px, brightness 91±2, sharpness 3184±290.
  • metal_nut: 700×700 px, brightness 59±4, sharpness 228±63.
  • screw: 1024×1024 px, brightness 184±6, sharpness 89±13.
  • Acquisition is tightly controlled (small brightness spread within a product). That is what lets a good-only model work — and why a lamp or focus change on the real line (Drift tab) is dangerous.
  • Test captures differ slightly from training captures (carpet test images are brighter and from a different roll) — handled by the lot re-qualification in the Drift & new lots tab.
  • Test sets are defect-heavy (≈70% defective) unlike a real line (≈1%). We therefore report rates per class and re-weight costs and review load to a 1% defect rate.

    Features beat pixels — for memory and for generation

    Mean image AUROC: PatchCore (CNN memory bank) 0.979 · PatchCore + VAE ensemble 0.978 · Feature-space VAE (GenAI) 0.899 · Pixel VAE (GenAI, v1) 0.683 · Aligned mean-image baseline 0.562. The pixel VAE redraws a blurry part, so subtle defects hide in its own error. Working on the frozen CNN's features — as a memory of normal patches (PatchCore) or as a VAE that reconstructs the feature map — keeps the local detail that separates defects.

    Operating point (PatchCore)

    At the synthetic-only threshold on the operating test split: false-reject rate 0.0%, escape rate 3.9%, human review load 16.6% of parts (prevalence-adjusted).

    Synthetic vs real threshold

    Cost-optimal threshold chosen with synthetic defects vs with real labelled defects (oracle): bottle: 39.0 vs 41.5, screw: 36.5 vs 33.0, carpet: 35.5 vs 37.0. Explore it in the Threshold & cost tab.

    5 · Responsible AI

    Human in the loop

    CHECK is a first-class outcome, not an error. Every CHECK enters the review queue; the inspector's verdict and note are logged with the model score, threshold and version. Heat maps show visual deviation, not root cause.

    Drift & new lots

    A dimming lamp, a dirty lens, a bumped camera or a new production lot shifts every image. A good-only model reads that as "unusual". We monitor camera-health signals and the score stream with EWMA control charts; a lot change is confirmed with a statistical test on a few good parts and handled by re-qualification — never by silent retraining.

    Limits & licence

    The score is a ranking, not a defect probability. Synthetic defects are a calibration tool, not proof of coverage — validate every critical defect mode on plant data. MVTec AD is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: research and teaching only.
